header.subject: Maths
header.title: Division concept + dividing mentally
header.goal: Children share a total into equal rings and say 24 ÷ 6 = 4.

moves.do: Say “24 is 20 and ___; 24 is 6 × ___”; class answers together.
moves.yesterday: Last chapter we wrote 6 groups of 4 = 24. What is 4 × 6? (24)

moves.how: Post: divide, total, groups, quotient. Who shares rotis?
moves.say: “Today we share a total into equal groups.”

moves.do: Draw 24 dots, ring them into 6 equal rings, count one ring: 4.
moves.think: I ring one at a time and count the ring: 4. Then I check the 6s: 6, 12, 18, 24, the fourth line. Same answer.

moves.do: Draw 18 gift boxes (p.66 Q2); class helps ring 9 equal rings.
moves.how: Count one ring. Volunteer writes 18 ÷ 9 = 2; check 9 × 2.

moves.do: One minute: show your rings; your neighbour checks the table.
moves.how: A: 32 stickers, 8 rings; B: 30 stars, 6. Sana and Ali show it first.
moves.say: “Show me the rings before you tell me the number.”

turn.a: I ringed 32 stickers into 8 rings. Check my 8s: one ring?
turn.b: Mine: 30 stars, 6 rings. Yours: 8 × 4 = 32. Check my 6s.

moves.do: Alone: 1. 35 prizes among 7 games, how many each? Draw, ring, write.
moves.how: Done? 2. 42 marbles, 6 friends; other shares, none left.

sections.mistake: Skips drawing or writes 7 ÷ 35. Ask: “Which number is the whole pile?”
sections.stuck: Give 12 bottle caps; child deals one per ring first.

moves.do: Say 40 pencils shared among 5 children; five say the sentence.
moves.how: Think alone, picture 5 rings; five say how many each and the ÷ sentence.
moves.say: “Picture your rings, then say the sentence.”

sections.success: I can share a total into equal rings and say ÷.
sections.ask: How can you check your answer by multiplying?
sections.listen: 5 rings of 8 dots: 5 × 8 gives the total, 40.

moves.do: Find one thing shared equally at home (rotis, eggs, sweets).
